title: capabilities/{id}/workflows.json — compiled intent micro-flows (ADR-005 Parts 2/4)
description: Facts, not behavior: slot lists, prompt references, validation instances bound to the closed predicate vocabulary, confirmation/completion wiring. Behavior kinds live in versioned runtimes (ADR-001.1 fact/behavior split).

entity.description: Capability-scoped or shared entity id (resolved by compiler stage 3).

validation.description: Instances of the closed predicate set; parameters type-checked at compile time (stage 1/2).

action.description: Action key from this capability's capability.json, same rule as `completion.action` (ADR-002 A9). The two are NOT interchangeable: `completion.action` is what the intent does when it needs no permission, these are what each answer to the question does.

label.description: OPTIONAL, compat only. The single name a host's intent table uses for this outcome — the Dialogflow-era `Cmd.SendMessage - yes`. Not a model class and not an intent id: polarity is decided after classification, so the head's label space cannot contain it. A client reports this instead of the intent id when present, and the intent id unchanged when absent. Drop the key when the host consumes plain intent ids; nothing else depends on it.

label.description: OPTIONAL, compat only. The single name a host's intent table uses for this outcome — the Dialogflow-era `Cmd.SendMessage - yes`. Not a model class and not an intent id: polarity is decided after classification, so the head's label space cannot contain it. confirmation.description: How this intent asks permission, and what each answer does. `yes`/`no` are OPTIONAL IN THIS SCHEMA ONLY so that packs signed before the branches existed still verify; they are not optional in practice. A pack that asks a question without stating both answers forces every client to invent them, and clients invent different things — VoiceAIKit took `completion.action` for yes and an empty action for no, which silently disagreed with the reference engine the moment content authored a decline with its own action. A runtime is entitled to REFUSE such a pack, and VoiceAIKit does. Emit both branches for anything built from here on; the golden example in spec/examples/3.0/full shows the complete shape.

action.description: Action key from this capability's capability.json (cross-capability references are a compile error — ADR-002 A9).

back_reference.description: Referent-table hook for corrections ('no, the other one').
